item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, but leaning no. Putin did elevate some real technocrats in 2024, most notably Andrei Belousov, yet the broader personnel pattern still centered on long-time loyalists, former bodyguards, and security insiders. I found no strong 2024 evidence of family members being placed into core governing posts, but I did find strong evidence of a loyalist inner circle and corruption-prone patronage networks.

The same reporting says Belousov was also loyal to Putin and had no independent political base, so this is only weak evidence for merit over patronage. | 7B.5, 7B.3 |

This is the best counterexample I found, but it is about macro policy, not a broader merit-based personnel system. | 7B.5, 7B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I found some real technocratic appointments in 2024, but they were embedded in a clear loyalist structure.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Putin built a genuinely merit-based cabinet insulated from security insiders, bodyguards, family ties, or patronage.
- I also did not find credible 2024 evidence of family members directly running core ministries; the pattern was loyalists, ex-security personnel, and trusted insiders rather than literal family rule.
